look_up_ip.description: Find out where an IPv4 or IPv6 address is (country, region, city, postcode, coordinates and UTC offset), which network it belongs to and whether it is a known proxy. Useful for tagging sign-ups or orders by country and for spotting visitors hiding behind a proxy. Private addresses come back with 'found' set to false rather than failing the step. No API key required.

mock_response.summary: 8.8.8.8 is in Mountain View, California, United States of America (Google LLC)

look_up_ip.name: look_up_ip

parameters.description: The IPv4 or IPv6 address to look up.
parameters.name: ip_address

asn.description: The number of the network (autonomous system) the address belongs to, e.g. 15169.

country_name.description: The country's name, e.g. 'United States of America'.

found.description: True when IP2Location could place the address. False for a private or reserved address (such as 10.0.0.1) or one it has no record of; every other detail is then empty.

ip.description: The address that was looked up, e.g. '8.8.8.8'.

is_proxy.description: True when IP2Location knows the address as a proxy (an open proxy, VPN, Tor exit and the like).

latitude.description: The latitude of the location, e.g. 37.38605.

longitude.description: The longitude of the location, e.g. -122.08385.

network_name.description: The name of the organisation that runs that network, e.g. 'Google LLC'.

postal_code.description: The ZIP or postal code of the area, e.g. '94043'.

region.description: The state, province or region, e.g. 'California'.

summary.description: One line saying where the address is, e.g. '8.8.8.8 is in Mountain View, California, United States of America (Google LLC)', or that no location was found.

utc_offset.description: The location's current offset from UTC, e.g. '-07:00'. It is an offset, not a time zone name, and moves with daylight saving.

description: Look up where an IPv4 or IPv6 address is with IP2Location.io: the country, region, city, postcode, coordinates and UTC offset, the network it belongs to and whether it is a known proxy. No account or API key required.
